newsitem.title: USA: Little left of crashed Illinois planes.
newsitem.headline: Little left of crashed Illinois planes.

text.p: A runway crash that killed 14 people in two planes caused a ferocious fire that left very little remaining, accident investigators said on Wednesday.
"There is very little left," said George Black of the National Transportation Safety Board. He called the fire which followed Thursday evening's collisison "vicious."
But investigators said they had located the cockpit voice recorder in the 19-seat Beech 1900, a twin-engine turboprop operated by Great Lakes Aviation for United Express.

United Express released the names of 10 passengers and two crew members on its flight from Chicago to Quincy via Burlington, Iowa. The two people in the smaller twin-prop Beech King Air 200 which struck the United Express flight as it was landing had not been identified.
Visibility at the airport -- which does not have a control tower -- was clear at the time of the collision at 6:02 p.m. EST, witnesses said.

The United Express aircraft had just come in for a landing, while the private plane was taking off from a perpendicular runway. Pilots at such unmanned airports are supposed to be in radio contact with each other.
Adams County Sheriff Robert Nall told reporters on Wednesday "people are going to ask themselves if it's safe to travel from here."
